status_summary: Executive Order 14168, signed 2025-01-20 and published 2025-01-30, requires agency forms that ask about sex to offer only male or female without a gender identity question, and directs removal of agency materials and forms that promote what it calls gender ideology. On 2025-02-25 a CDC spokesperson told STAT that CDC would stop processing transgender identity data to comply with the order, that the Youth Risk Behavior Survey was being modified, and that sexual orientation data would continue to be processed; STAT also reported that removed webpages and datasets were restored after a court order. A September 2026 report on the 2025 Youth Risk Behavior Survey says the shorter national report omitted several topics found in earlier reports.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14168 signed; it requires agency forms that ask about sex to offer only male or female and not to request gender identity (published 2025-01-30).
CDC tells a health news outlet that it will stop processing transgender identity data to comply with the executive order; sexual orientation data is unaffected.

title: End CDC collection of gender identity data
uncertainties: The CDC step rests on one outlet quoting a CDC spokesperson; no CDC notice or survey instrument was read. The court order restoring webpages is known only from secondary reporting, and which surveys (BRFSS, YRBS, HIV surveillance) dropped the item is not confirmed from CDC documents.
